chunks: He said: I asked him about the Month of Ramadan, how much is prayed in it. He said: “As is prayed in it.” He said: “As is prayed in other than it, except that the Month of Ramadan has, over all the other months, such merit that it is fitting for the servant to increase in his voluntary prayer.

So if he wishes and has strength for that, he may increase in the first part of the month up to twenty nights, praying each night twenty rak'ahs in addition to what he used to pray before that. Of these twenty, he prays twelve rak'ahs between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight rak'ahs after 'Isha. Then he prays the night prayer that he used to pray before that: eight, and the witr is three; he prays two rak'ahs and gives taslim in them, then stands and prays one, making qunut in it, and that is the witr. Then he prays the two rak'ahs of Fajr until dawn breaks, so these are thirteen rak'ahs.

Then when ten nights remain of the Month of Ramadan, let him pray thirty rak'ahs in every night besides these thirteen. Of them, he prays twenty-two rak'ahs between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight rak'ahs after 'Isha. Then he prays the night prayer of thirteen rak'ahs as I have described to you.

And on the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third, in each one of them, if he has strength for that, he prays one hundred rak'ahs besides these thirteen rak'ahs. And let him remain awake in them until morning, for it is recommended that this be in prayer, supplication, and humble entreaty, for it is hoped that Laylat al-Qadr may be in one of them.”

ai.seo_question: How many recommended prayers are performed in the Month of Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the recommended increase in voluntary salat (prayer) during the Month of Ramadan, especially in its final ten nights. It details the number and timing of rak'ahs, highlights the merit of remaining awake in worship and du'a, and points to the special hope associated with Laylat al-Qadr.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1967 – Imam (as) was asked about the prayer during the Month of Ramadan and said:
"It is prayed as in other months. However, Month of Ramadan holds additional merit over other months, so it is appropriate for a servant to increase their voluntary prayers.

If one desires and has the strength, they may add twenty rak'ahs each night during the first twenty nights, in addition to what they usually pray. Of these twenty rak'ahs, twelve are prayed between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight after 'Isha. Then, the usual night prayer is prayed, consisting of eight rak'ahs, followed by the three rak'ahs of witr: two rak'ahs with a taslim, then a single rak'ah with qunut, completing the witr. Afterward, the two rak'ahs of Fajr are prayed until dawn breaks, making thirteen rak'ahs in total.

When ten nights remain in Month of Ramadan, thirty rak'ahs may be prayed each night, apart from these thirteen rak'ahs. Of these thirty rak'ahs, twenty-two are prayed between Maghrib and 'Isha, and eight after 'Isha. Then, the night prayer of thirteen rak'ahs is prayed as previously described.

On the nights of the 21st and 23rd, if one has the strength, one may pray one hundred rak'ahs in each of these nights, apart from the thirteen rak'ahs. Let them stay awake until morning in prayer, supplication, and humility, as it is hoped that one of these nights will be Laylat al-Qadr."
